title: Process 3D Technology And App
description: Create a new technology `process` with part `3d` for simulating processing of components through subtractive and additive measures (cutting, drilling, attachments), built on the repo's brep kernel (kernel_3d_brepkit). Add a vcs-backed document crate process/3d/rs, a plugin app process/plugin/rs (app id process3d-play, World3d viewport), example fixtures, AGENTS.md seeds, and register the new technology across Cargo.toml, package.json, repo/lib/js/index.ts, framework/core/js/index.ts, .claude/launch.json, and s/manifest/resources.manifest.json.
summary:
Created the new `process` technology and its `3d` app for simulating component processing (subtractive cuts/drills and additive attachments) through the repo's brep kernel (kernel_3d_brepkit). Added a vcs-backed document crate `process/3d/rs` (Process3dDocument model with Stock/ProcessStep/ProcessMeasure, using vcs's CollectionOp/Identified/Patchable pattern for undoable step-list edits, 5 unit tests). Added the plugin app `process/plugin/rs` (app id process3d-play) with a World3d "Workpiece" viewport driven by a memoized BrepkitKernel replay session (cut_sync/fuse_sync per step), document/catalogue/inspector panels, undo/redo, cursor scrubbing through the process timeline, EN/DE terminology, and 11 unit tests. Added two example fixtures (timber beam with miter cuts + dowel joinery, drilled plate) and AGENTS.md seeds for the new technology. Registered the technology across the workspace: Cargo.toml, package.json, repo/lib/js/index.ts (playground aliases/ports), framework/core/js/index.ts (registry ids), .claude/launch.json (process3d-react-dev, port 6022), and s/manifest/resources.manifest.json. Verified: cargo check/test pass for both crates (16/16 tests), wasm build succeeds, plugin registry auto-discovery picks up the new component, and the app was manually driven end-to-end in the browser (viewport renders the kernel-tessellated beam, document tree shows stock+steps with correct icons, inspector edits round-trip through the kernel and update the model with no console errors).

Note: mid-task an accidental `git stash`/`git stash pop` popped an unrelated pre-existing stash (someone else's "Auto stash before merge" WIP) and caused merge conflicts across ~15 unrelated files (hooks configs, README, bun.lock, script.ts, etc.). This was fully recovered: all conflicted files were restored to clean HEAD content, stash-only new files were removed, and the original stash entry (stash@{0}) was left fully intact and untouched in the stash list for its rightful owner to recover. No committed history was altered and none of this session's own changes were affected.
